Need to search first.I couldn't write the commentary notes this time, because my research tools stopped working before I read any of the sources.

My first attempt to open the pages for Psalm 69 directly was refused, because the tool only opens addresses that have first come up in a search. When I then tried to run the searches, the tool told me I had run out of calls for this turn. So I haven't read any page on Psalm 69 from Enduring Word, Bible Hub, StudyLight, Precept Austin, the NET Bible, New Advent or any other site on your list.

Your rules say to report only what I've read and to give a URL for every point. I have nothing that meets that, so I've left every verse blank rather than fill the gaps from memory.

**What I'd do next time** (just ask me again, for example "continue the Psalm 69 research"):
1. **Traditional reading:** search for and read the verse-by-verse pages on Psalm 69 from Enduring Word, Bible Hub (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary), Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*, Precept Austin and Wesley's notes.
2. **Verses Christians often discuss:**
   - The New Testament uses of the psalm: v. 4 in John 15:25, v. 9 in John 2:17 and Romans 15:3, v. 21 at the crucifixion, vv. 22–23 in Romans 11:9–10, and v. 25 in Acts 1:20.
   - The curses against enemies in vv. 22–28.
   - Being "blotted out of the Book of Life" (v. 28), which may bear on the Reformed versus Wesleyan/Methodist debate over whether salvation can be lost.
   - How the confession of "folly" and "guilt" in v. 5 fits a reading of the psalm as being about Christ.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes; Augustine's exposition of this psalm on New Advent (numbered Psalm 68 in his Bible); Catholic.com and OCA material; GotQuestions on the psalms that curse enemies.

I'd treat those verses only as places to look. I'll report a Protestant disagreement or another view only if the pages I read actually show it, with the URL for each point.
